title: Fault family — collection element-count containment (mincount/maxcount) across a mutation or a default list

mintSites.howMinted: engine-synthesized, NO catalog ProofRequirements slot: WalkActions (ProofEngine.cs:505) calls CountContainmentObligation for every action on every write plan. It reads the field's DeclaredMinCount/DeclaredMaxCount and the action's catalog ActionEffectClass (Grows/Shrinks/Empties/ReplacesValue), advances a single per-field count interval seeded once from the governed band [mincount ?? 0, maxcount ?? ∞], and stamps a CountContainmentProofRequirement carrying the post-mutation interval. Prove-or-reject: DiagnosticCode.CountBoundViolation (PRE0136) unless the interval is provably in-band.

engine-synthesized, NO catalog slot: CollectCountDefaultObligation (called at ProofEngine.Analysis.cs:445) stamps a CountContainmentProofRequirement for a count-bounded field whose `default [...]` is a TypedListLiteral, with the exact literal element count as the point interval [n, n], against the declared mincount/maxcount. This is the establishment (construction) base case that the mutation cells' premise (d) inductive hypothesis rests on.

notes: Every sound-but-unprovable band member respells into a licensed form. The band is spellings the seed-narrowing (SeedCountInterval) does not read: a guard on a proxy variable rather than on `F.count` (e.g. `when NotFull` where NotFull tracks count < max); an algebraically-rearranged count comparison (`when F.count + 1 <= maxcount`, which SeedCountInterval does not parse — it reads only `F.count op literal`). The licensed respelling of each is a direct `when F.count < maxcount` (or `> mincount`) guard, or an adjusted mincount/maxcount declaration, or a routed `when F.count >= maxcount -> reject` sibling.

SeedCountInterval reads both `<` and `<=` (and `>`, `>=`, `==`), so `when F.count <= maxcount - 1` and `when F.count < maxcount` are BOTH licensed — neither is a band member; the boundary that separates a band member from a licensed spelling is whether the guard's comparison is literally `F.count op integer-literal`.

cells.label: Count containment at a transition-row mutating action — post-mutation count must stay within [mincount, maxcount]

coordinates.operationKind: count-containment on a mutating collection action (Grows/Shrinks/Empties per ActionEffectClass)

metavariables.name: F
metavariables.standsFor: the count-bounded collection field the action mutates

normalization.note: the Normalization bullet — the count domain is integer, so guard/sibling narrowing is exact

wp.statement: AdvanceCount(seed, delta) ⊆ [mincount, maxcount], where seed = narrow([mincount ?? 0, maxcount ?? ∞], guard, reject-siblings) and delta is the action's catalog per-kind count effect (grow: upper +1, lower +1 or +0 for a dedup kind; shrink: lower −1 floored 0, upper −1 or +0 for a conditional no-op; clear: reset to [0,0])
wp.note: prove-or-reject: clean iff AdvanceCount(seed,delta).lower >= mincount AND .upper <= maxcount (ProofRequirement.cs:227-235). A `set` to a non-literal drops the tracked interval and mints nothing (re-seeds on the next grow).

cells.premiseAvailability: Every discharge consumes (a) AND (d): (a) the field's declared mincount/maxcount define the band AND — via governance holding count in [mincount, maxcount] at chain entry — the endpoints of the seed; (d) the inductive hypothesis that the count was in-band before this handler ran IS the seed. (c) applies whenever the transition row carries a `F.count op literal` conjunct in its `when` guard (narrows the seed via SeedCountInterval). A routed reject-row sibling (`when F.count op N -> reject` above this row) narrows the seed as a discharge MECHANISM (predecessor exclusion, BuildSiblingCountExclusions) — available at this occasion only. Class (b) never applies: the count delta is a fixed per-action constant; no event argument represents a collection's cardinality, and the grown value's own arg constraints bound WHAT is added, not HOW MANY.

dischargeContract.derivation: structural headroom: the seed [mincount ?? 0, maxcount ?? ∞] advanced by the action's per-kind delta already lands in-band without any guard — a grow when F has no maxcount (upper stays ∞) or a shrink when F has no mincount (lower floored 0 = effective mincount).
dischargeContract.decisionProcedure: Integer interval arithmetic: seed = [mincount ?? 0, maxcount ?? ∞]; post = AdvanceCount(seed, delta); accept iff post.lower >= mincount AND post.upper <= maxcount. Finite, no search. (live-observed: mincount-1 field grown by append → band [1..∞], Proved/CountContainment.)

citations.note: Inductive hypothesis plus sign monotonicity — here the monotone step is the catalog per-kind count delta (a grow raises count, a shrink lowers it), not the numeric subtraction of Family 1 Base B; the pre-state fact is the count-in-band inductive hypothesis

dischargeContract.derivation: a `F.count op literal` conjunct in the row's `when` guard narrows the seed (SeedCountInterval: `< N` caps upper at N−1, `> N` raises lower to N+1, `== N` pins both) so that the delta-advanced interval lands in-band. Example: `when F.count < maxcount` gives a grow the headroom it structurally lacks.
dischargeContract.decisionProcedure: Extract `F.count op integer-literal` conjuncts from the row guard (per-branch union across an OR guard, so an OR never over-narrows — SeedCountInterval:697-724); tighten the seed; run the same interval arithmetic. A guard on a proxy variable or an algebraically-rearranged comparison is NOT extracted (a band member, respellable). (live-observed: `when Items.count < 3` on a maxcount-3 grow → Proved; weakening to `when Items.count <= 3` → PRE0136, same obligation.)

transport.earnedAt: phase 2, immediately after the row guard evaluates (transport-rule § 5, Fired-guard fact)
transport.consumedAt: the mutating action (phase 5 of the operation execution order — the row's mutation chain)
transport.killCondition: the fact is killed if any construct on the route between the guard evaluation and the mutation writes F. For a transition row this includes a source-state EXIT action (phase 3, which runs BEFORE the row's action chain — the 2026-07-21 soundness correction) that grows/shrinks/clears F. SeedCountInterval narrows from the guard WITHOUT a frame-and-kill check against such interposing writers — see openFlags.

citations.note: route-indexed frame-and-kill: deps(φ) ∩ mayWrite(r, p, q) = ∅

citations.ref: docs/Working/transport-rule-restatement-2026-07-21.md § 7. What kills — the write set and the read-closure
citations.note: collection grow/shrink/clear and the exit-action chain are writers of the collection field
Arg-bound interval arithmetic, guard-spelled variant: the per-term bound conjuncts feed the same interval arithmetic; inherits the 2026-07-21 no-intervening-write soundness correction

dischargeContract.derivation: a reject-row sibling `when F.count op N -> reject` declared ABOVE this row on the same (state, event) intercepts those cases first, so this fall-through row fires only when the sibling guard is FALSE; the integer negation caps the seed (e.g. `when F.count >= N -> reject` ⇒ this row fires with F.count <= N−1). The narrowed seed advanced by the delta lands in-band.
dischargeContract.decisionProcedure: BuildSiblingCountExclusions (ProofEngine.cs:761-820): single-leaf `F.count op integer-literal` reject guards above the current row, matched on event + FromState compatibility + first-match position, negated into an integer count band, intersected. Then the same interval arithmetic. (live-observed: `when Items.count >= 3 -> reject` above an unguarded append to a maxcount-3 list → Proved/CountContainment.)
dischargeContract.note: This is a discharge MECHANISM, not a premise class (matrix § Vocabulary — Discharge mechanisms). It is available at transition-row-action-operand ONLY: siblingCountCaps is null for state hooks and stateless handlers (ProofEngine.cs:434-436).

transport.earnedAt: phase 2, at each earlier sibling row's guard evaluation (transport-rule § 5, Predecessor exclusion)
transport.killCondition: same interposing-writer hazard as the guard case; additionally, transport-rule § 5 flags predecessor exclusion as unavailable on inspect-fire routes (a shrink of the fault surface routed to the owner, N8).

citations.ref: docs/Working/transport-rule-restatement-2026-07-21.md § 5. What earns a fact, and on which routes
citations.note: Predecessor exclusion — earned at the earlier guard; the surviving inspect-fire restriction is routed (N8)
transition rows are first-match — the fall-through row fires only when every earlier sibling guard was false

dischargeContract.pruningDerivation: empty: class (b) × count-containment. The action's count delta is a fixed per-kind catalog constant (grow +1/+0, shrink −1/−0, clear→0) independent of every event argument; no argument represents F's cardinality, and an argument bounding the grown VALUE (`append F Arg` with Arg constrained) bounds what is added, never how many. No arg-constraint premise can appear in the discharge, so class (b) is pruned, not merely unavailable-here.

citations.note: the per-kind delta is derived from ActionEffectClass and TypeMeta.DeduplicatesElements — no arg is read

citationDuty.establishingObligation: the field-default (or construction) count-establishment obligation — cell fault-countcontainment-field-default-collection — proves the count is in-band in the initial configuration
citationDuty.preservingObligations: every OTHER mutating action of F, in every write plan (this cell at every occasion), each carrying its own CountContainment obligation that keeps the count in-band
citationDuty.status: NOT dischargeable as a cited proof today — the citation-duty machinery (naming establishing + preserving obligations in the certificate) is unbuilt, and the ProofRequirement DU carries no establishment/preservation subtype (matrix § Obligation family). Today the seed consumes the count-in-band assumption BARE. suggestions.schema: add a `when F.count op N` guard giving the mutation direction headroom (`< maxcount` for a grow, `> mincount` for a shrink)
widen the declared maxcount (or lower the mincount) so the un-narrowed seed advanced by the delta lands in-band

base.program:
precept CountTransitionBase

field Items as list of integer maxcount 3 default [1, 2]

state Cart initial

event Add(Value as integer)

from Cart on Add
    -> append Items Add.Value
    -> no transition

expected.diagnostic: PRE0136 (CountBoundViolation) — cannot prove Items stays within maxcount 3 after this add

provenance.head: c295d7b4
provenance.note: syntax + observed compiler behavior; the definition (not the compiler's verdict) is the authority — they agree here

discharges.derivation: guard narrows seed to [0,2]; grow → [1,3]; upper 3 <= maxcount 3 → in-band

discharges.addition: declare the field `mincount 1` and no maxcount (grow can never breach an absent upper)
discharges.derivation: seed [1,∞]; grow → [2,∞]; lower 2 >= mincount 1, no upper → in-band without any guard

discharges.addition: from Cart on Add when Items.count >= 3 -> reject "Cart is full" (above the append row)
discharges.derivation: sibling caps this row's seed upper at 2; grow → [1,3]; upper 3 <= maxcount 3 → in-band

nearMisses.whyStillRejects: `<= 3` caps the seed upper at 3 (not 2); grow → [1,4]; upper 4 > maxcount 3 — the guard is weakened past sufficiency, must still reject the same obligation

nearMisses.addition: declare the sibling reject row BELOW the append row instead of above it — `from Cart on Add -> append …` first, then `from Cart on Add when Items.count >= 3 -> reject`.
nearMisses.whyStillRejects: the exclusion depends on the reject row preceding the append on the same (state, event): rows are tried in order, so only a reject declared above intercepts the over-cap case before the append runs. Below it, the append is reached first and nothing has excluded a full cart.

nearMisses.addition: supply an upper bound the grow can reach — declare `mincount 1 maxcount 1` instead of `mincount 1` with no maxcount.
nearMisses.whyStillRejects: the absent upper bound was doing all the work: with no maxcount there is no upper band for a grow to breach, so headroom is structural. Supplying a maxcount the append can exceed restores the obligation, and with no guard narrowing the seed the delta-advanced interval leaves the band.

citations.note: the transition-row-action-operand occasion; siblingCountCaps computed here (ProofEngine.cs:434-436)

notes: The site-identity ruling (matrix § The minting rule) makes this obligation per-occasion: one append reached by two transitions into the same handler mints two obligations, each proved from its own route's facts. The shipped compiler mints one per action per handler (route-collapsed); route-splitting is the transport-rule restatement's committed change, parked.

None of the three witnesses use `dequeue ... into` or any of the uncatalogued writers, so none rests on BUG-033 or the write-surface enumeration gap — they are verified, not flagged. The DEPENDENCY on that enumeration is real for premise (d) and is recorded in citationDuty + openFlags.

cells.label: Count containment of a default list literal — establishment at construction

metavariables.name: F
metavariables.standsFor: the count-bounded collection field carrying a `default [...]`

metavariables.name: n
metavariables.standsFor: the exact element count of the default list literal (a compile-time constant)

wp.statement: the point interval [n, n] ⊆ [mincount, maxcount]; i.e. mincount <= n AND n <= maxcount. n is the literal's element count (exact, no interval widening).

cells.premiseAvailability: ONLY class (a): the field's own declared mincount/maxcount, checked against the constant-folded literal count. There is NO pre-state (this IS the initial configuration), so class (d) does not apply; no guard on a default, so class (c) does not apply; no arguments, so class (b) does not apply. This cell is the ESTABLISHMENT base case that the three mutation cells' premise (d) inductive hypothesis cites.

dischargeContract.derivation: constant-fold the default list literal's element count n; the field's declared mincount/maxcount is checked directly against the point interval [n, n]. Discharges iff n is in-band.
dischargeContract.decisionProcedure: n = list.Elements.Length (ProofEngine.Analysis.cs:701, exact); accept iff n >= (mincount ?? 0) AND (maxcount is null OR n <= maxcount). Finite, no search, no widening. (live-observed: `default [1,2,3]` with maxcount 2 → PRE0136; `default [1,2]` → Proved/CountContainment.)

citations.note: Literal constant-fold for defaults — construction builds the hollow version with defaults applied; the default surface takes a literal; a list literal's element count is exact, so the fold compares an exact count against the declared band

dischargeContract.pruningDerivation: empty: a construction default has no pre-state (no d), no guard (no c), and no event arguments (no b). The only fact available is the field's own declared band (a). This is why the establishment base case is a pure constant-fold — it cannot borrow an inductive hypothesis, which is exactly why it must hold unconditionally for the mutation cells' (d) to be sound.

citations.note: Establishment over defaults / the pre-configuration rule — establishment WP is taken over the default configuration

citationDuty.establishingObligation: none — this cell IS the establishing obligation for F's count invariant
citationDuty.status: self-contained; the only consumed fact is the field's own declared band, established by the declaration itself. This cell supplies the establishing obligation that the mutation cells must cite under the 2026-07-21 citation duty.

suggestions.schema: make the default list have between mincount and maxcount elements, or adjust the declared mincount/maxcount to admit the default's count
